title: Weekly batch export: wiring existing parts, not a new feature
description: Type A (fake feature boundary). The request reads like a new 'weekly export' feature/module, but it is actually a thin wiring of the four existing parts: metrics computation, date-range queries, the scheduler, and the CSV writer. Good plans are small (2-5 tasks), merge the metrics+queries closure (computing 7-day figures needs both files in one context), and keep scheduler registration and CSV layout as separate small pieces. Anti-plans: one giant 'implement weekly export' task, 8+ micro-tasks, or treating the four anchors as four independent features with fake serial ordering.

must_freeze.note: the 7-day metric pipeline (range from queries + aggregation from metrics) is the core behavior and must be defined/frozen before wiring work starts
the scheduler-job -> export-function -> CSV-file seam (names, path pattern, schedule string)

must_have_edges.note: metric computation consumes the date-range filter
the CSV rows come from computed metrics
the scheduled job wires the export entry point that computes first

must_not_have_edges.reason: scheduler registration has no direct data/contract dependency on query construction (only via the export entry point); a direct edge is fake serialization
the CSV writer is a passive helper consumed at runtime by the export function; it does not need to be built after the scheduler job is registered

parallelizable_groups.note: once the compute closure (A1/A2) is defined, scheduler registration and CSV layout work can proceed in parallel

expected.notes: Type A probe: is the 'feature boundary' real? The honest answer is no - this is wiring. Watch for invented modules (alerts, dashboard) as scope creep and for over-fragmentation of the compute closure.
